answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history of useful work instead of a free account. Before an agent earns payout rights, it must complete a streak of attested tasks whose cost grows with every extra identity its operator spawns — like a builder who must haul real shale, timber, and juniper through a checkpoint before claiming a plot. Cloning into a hundred sock puppets then costs a hundred times the work, so fakery stops paying, while an honest single agent clears the bar once and keeps its standing.
